timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for a simple “IP → Company + Contact” API. I’ll show you one of the most popular public services (ipinfo.io) and a few alternatives so you can pick the one that best fits your needs. --- ## 1. ipinfo.io – The “go‑to” service | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Endpoint** | `https://ipinfo.io//json` | | **Auth** | Free tier: no key needed for up to 50k requests/day.
Paid plans: API key via `?token=YOUR_TOKEN` or `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN`. | | **Response fields** | `hostname`, `city`, `region`, `country`, `loc`, `org`, `postal`, `timezone`, `readme`, **plus** optional `company` object when available. | | **Company object** | `{ "name": "...", "domain": "...", "type": "...", "industry": "...", "description": "...", "logo": "...", "phone": "...", "website": "...", "address": "...", "city": "...", "state": "...", "country": "...", "postal": "...", "latitude": "...", "longitude": "..." }` | | **Rate limits** | 50 000 req/day (free). Paid tiers increase limits and add features like bulk lookups. | ### Example request ```bash curl -s https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json ``` ### Example response ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth", "company": { "name": "Google LLC", "domain": "google.com", "type": "Internet Service Provider", "industry": "Technology", "description": "Google LLC is an American multinational technology company.", "logo": "https://ipinfo.io/static/img/logo.png", "phone": "+1-650-253-0000", "website": "https://www.google.com", "address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway", "city": "Mountain View", "state": "CA", "country": "US", "postal": "94043", "latitude": "37.4220", "longitude": "-122.0841" } } ``` > **Tip:** If the `company` field is missing, the IP either belongs to a residential ISP or the data isn’t available in the free tier. --- ## 2. Alternative APIs | Service | Endpoint | Key | Notes | |---------|----------|-----|-------| | **ipapi.co** | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | `?key=YOUR_KEY` | Free tier: 30 000 req/month. Includes `org`, `asn`, `company` (if available). | | **ipstack.com** | `http://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=YOUR_KEY` | Required | Paid plans start at $10/mo. Returns `organization`, `company_name`, `company_website`, `company_phone`. | | **ipgeolocation.io** | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=` | Required | Free tier: 1 000 req/day. Provides `isp`, `organization`, `company_name`, `company_website`, `company_address`. | | **ipdata.co** | `https://api.ipdata.co/?api-key=YOUR_KEY` | Required | Free tier: 1 500 req/day. Returns `organization`, `company_name`, `company_website`, `company_address`. | All of them return similar fields; just check the docs for exact naming conventions. --- ## 3. Quick Python example (using `requests`) ```python import requests def get_ip_info(ip, token=None): url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" params = {"token": token} if token else {} resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() # Pull out company info if present company = data.get("company") if company: print(f"Company: {company['name']}") print(f"Phone: {company.get('phone', 'N/A')}") print(f"Website: {company.get('website', 'N/A')}") else: print("No company data available for this IP.") # Example usage get_ip_info("8.8.8.8") # No token needed for free tier # get_ip_info("8.8.8.8", token="YOUR_TOKEN") # For paid tier ``` --- ## 4. Things to keep in mind | Issue | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Privacy** | Some IPs belong to private networks or VPNs; company data may be generic or missing. | | **Accuracy** | Data is sourced from WHOIS and other registries; it’s usually reliable but can lag behind real‑time changes. | | **Legal** | Always respect the terms of service. Don’t scrape or store data beyond what the provider allows. | | **Caching** | IP geolocation rarely changes. Cache responses for 24–48 h to stay within rate limits. | --- ## 5. Summary * **ipinfo.io** is the easiest to start with—no key for up to 50 k requests/day, and it returns a rich `company` object when available. * If you need higher limits or more detailed company fields, consider **ipapi.co**, **ipstack.com**, or **ipgeolocation.io**. * All services expose a simple JSON endpoint; just parse the `company` (or equivalent) field for contact info. Happy coding! 🚀
